title: Weight, mass & g
examples: Teacher, if I go to the Moon, will my mass change?
What is the difference between my mass and my weight?
Does the strength of gravity change on different planets?

explain.say: Today we will learn about weight and mass. Say what you think weight means.
Weight is the force of gravity on an object. Gravity pulls things towards the Earth. We measure weight in Newtons.
The formula for weight is weight equals mass times the acceleration due to gravity. This is written as W equals m times g.
Mass is the amount of stuff in an object. It stays the same no matter where you are. We measure mass in kilograms.

items: Mass is the amount of stuff.

explain.say: On the Moon, gravity is weaker than on Earth. So your weight will be less, but your mass stays the same. For example, if your mass is sixty kilograms, your weight on the Moon will be much less.

faq.q: If I travel to another planet, will my weight change?
faq.a: Yes, your weight will change because the planet has a different gravitational pull. The strength of gravity affects your weight.
asks: Will my weight be different on Mars?

faq.q: Is mass the same as weight?
faq.a: No, they are different. Mass is a measure of how much matter you have. Weight is a force pulling on that mass.
asks: What is the difference between m and W?
Are mass and weight the same thing?

faq.q: What is the value of g on Earth?
faq.a: On Earth, the acceleration due to gravity, or g, is approximately nine point point eight meters per second squared. This value is used in calculations.
asks: What is the value of g?
How strong is gravity on Earth?

faq.q: If I lose weight, does my mass change?
faq.a: No, losing weight means you are losing something else, like fat. Your actual mass, the amount of matter you are made of, does not change just because you lose weight.
asks: Does weight loss mean mass loss?
Can I lose mass by dieting?

faq.q: How do I calculate my weight if I know my mass?
faq.a: You multiply your mass in kilograms by the value of g for that location. Remember the formula is W equals m times g.
asks: What is the formula for weight?
How do I find weight from mass?

facts: Weight is a force, measured in Newtons.
Mass is the amount of matter in an object, measured in kilograms.
The formula relating them is Weight equals mass times g.
The value of g changes depending on the planet or moon you are on.

quiz.say: A person has a mass of fifty kilograms on Earth. What is their approximate weight?
quiz.why: Weight is calculated by multiplying mass by the gravitational constant g, so fifty times nine point eight equals four hundred ninety Newtons.

wrong.0: This confuses the unit of mass with the unit of force.
wrong.1: This only uses the value of g and ignores the person's mass.
wrong.3: This forgets to multiply by the gravitational pull of Earth.

quiz.say: If you take your mass to the Moon, what happens to your mass value?
quiz.why: Mass measures the amount of matter you have, and that amount does not change when you travel to another celestial body.

wrong.0: This has no physical basis related to weightlessness or gravity.
wrong.2: This incorrectly assumes that gravity affects the amount of matter inside you.
wrong.3: This suggests that the Moon has no gravity at all.

quiz.say: Which quantity is measured in kilograms?
quiz.why: Kilograms are the standard unit used to measure mass, which is the amount of matter present in an object.

wrong.0: Force is a push or a pull, and its unit is the Newton.
wrong.1: Acceleration is a rate of change of velocity, measured in meters per second squared.
wrong.3: Weight is a force, so it must be measured in Newtons.
